The snapshot project contains no dimred_mbl_fnd_tfe_*, cmr_tfe_*, testForm_extension or reused declaration. So no snapshot declaration is reused, and the fresh names collide with nothing. Snapshot Mathlib supplies every library fact the children and the parent assembly use, and all of them resolve after import GMT.Ch07.Submission (Lean compile): HasCompactSupport.continuous_extend_zero, extend_zero and tsupport_extend_zero_subset (to_additive of Support.lean:341/327/321); exists_open_between_and_isCompact_closure (Regular.lean:364); cauchySeq_tendsto_of_complete (Cauchy.lean:425); HasCompactSupport.exists_bound_of_continuous (Bounded.lean:98); tendsto_one_div_add_atTop_nhds_zero_nat; tsupport_smul_subset_right; squeeze_zero_norm. rationale:
Split into four children: one reused accepted theorem and three new nodes.

1. Why split.
- A leaf may append exactly one theorem and no helper declarations (leaf_verification.check_source_delta). Unsplit, this proof would be a single declaration of about 330 lines.
- The supplied proof bundles three distinct, reusable analytic obligations:
  (A) uniform approximation of continuous compactly supported covector fields by test forms with prescribed support (step 3);
  (B) the Cauchy estimate and the choice-independent limit of T along such approximations (steps 4–5);
  (C) the linear extension Φ of T to compactly supported continuous fields on ℝ^P, with agreement on test forms and a local bound (steps 2–3, 5–8). This is the standard extension of a current with locally finite mass.
- The parent keeps only the zero extension g ↦ g̃ (steps 1, 7, 8) and the instantiation of the mass bound.

2. Children. The graph is acyclic, and the children sit at depth 5 (limit 6).
- mollify_unit_field: the accepted dor_ims_sua_mollify_unit_field (candidate 8abce32, closure accepted), with an identical frozen type. It is already a prerequisite of this node. It is listed as a child so that uniform_approx's worktree overlays it (runtime._overlay_accepted_children uses only a node's own children and depends_on).
- uniform_approx (dimred_mbl_fnd_tfe_uniform_testForm_approx): depends on mollify_unit_field.
- limit_functional (dimred_mbl_fnd_tfe_exists_limit_functional): no dependencies.
- ambient_extension (dimred_mbl_fnd_tfe_ambient_extension): depends on uniform_approx and limit_functional.

3. Mass-bound interface.
- limit_functional and ambient_extension take an arbitrary m : Set (Euclid P) → ℝ, with exactly the shape of eval_mass_bound's conclusion.
- The parent instantiates m W := (T.massOn W).toReal and discharges the hypothesis with its own accepted prerequisite cmr_abs_apply_le_massOn (candidate 7a70616). So that theorem does not need to be a child.
- Deviations from the supplied prose (each stated in a Source line):
  - (d) applies the m-bound to approximants of size r + 1/(k+1), rather than le_massOn to unit-size ±ω_k. The two estimates agree after rescaling.
  - The parent's (ii) chooses W ⊂⊂ U with exists_open_between_and_isCompact_closure. This is equivalent to the supplied thickening construction, which ambient_extension's step 2(i) states in full.

4. Names and the duplicate branch.
- The identical selected type is frozen at root.compactness_of_minimizing_currents-a1.mass_representation-a1.testform_extension-a1 (cmr_testForm_extension_functional, status decomposing).
- Its audited decomposition-v1 has these four children. Only its uniform_approx node (cmr_tfe_uniform_testForm_approx) is registered, and that node is unaccepted and under another parent. So _existing_lean_name_problem requires fresh names.
- The three new nodes keep those audited types byte for byte, under globally unique names dimred_mbl_fnd_tfe_* (no match in dag.json or the snapshot).

5. Parent assembly (this node's proof after the split; compiled).
 a. hbound W ω r hW hWU := cmr_abs_apply_le_massOn P n U W T ω r (hfin W hW hWU).ne. Obtain Φ with (a)–(d) from ambient_extension with m W := (T.massOn W).toReal.
 b. Define g̃ := Function.extend Subtype.val (fun x => c.symm (g x)) 0.
  - g̃ is continuous (HasCompactSupport.continuous_extend_zero; U is open).
  - g̃ has compact support (HasCompactSupport.extend_zero).
  - tsupport g̃ ⊆ val''(tsupport g) ⊆ U (tsupport_extend_zero_subset, tsupport_comp_subset).
  - g̃(x) = c⁻¹(g⟨x,hx⟩) on U and 0 off U. Hence (g₁+g₂)~ = g̃₁ + g̃₂ and (t•g)~ = t•g̃.
 c. L g := Φ g̃ is ℝ-linear by (a) and (b).
 d. (i): g̃ = ω, so L g = Φ ω = T ω by (c).
 e. (ii): choose an open W ⊇ val''K whose closure is compact and contained in U. Put M := 1·(T.massOn W).toReal. Then tsupport g̃ ⊆ val''K ⊆ W and |g̃| ≤ 1, so (d) with r = 1 gives |L g| ≤ M.

6. Lean verification. Every check ran with lake env lean in the workspace, in the comparator scope that verifier/gmt-compare.py contract_scope replays.
- /tmp/dmf-tfe-split/Types.lean: all child types, the parent type and the eval_mass_bound type elaborate.
- Parent.lean: the parent compiles from child stubs.
- ChildUA.lean, ChildLF.lean, ChildAE.lean: each child compiles from its sibling stubs; limit_functional needs none.
- E2E.lean (sha256 6b088bbf…): a sorry-free chain that includes the real accepted proofs from 7a70616 and 8abce32, the three new children and the parent. It also closes all six frozen types comparator-style with exact Submission.X. #print axioms reports only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. The proofs are 41, 102 and 110 lines for the children and 72 for the parent.
- Thick.lean: checks the thickening argument of ambient_extension step 2(i).
- All types pass lean_contract.validate_lean_statement.
- An independent reviewer agent re-ran E2E and byte-compared every type against E2E, the handoff and dag.json. It accepted all four children; both of its wording fixes are applied.

subproblems.title: Uniform smooth approximation of continuous unit covector fields (accepted theorem, reused)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n be natural numbers, Λ := Covector (Euclid P) n with operator norm ‖·‖, and |·| := covectorEuclideanNorm. Let V ⊆ ℝ^P be open. Let g : ℝ^P → Λ be continuous with compact support, tsupport g ⊆ V and |g(x)| ≤ 1 for every x. Let ε > 0. Then there is an n-form ω : ℝ^P → Λ that is C^∞ with compact support (IsTestForm ω), with tsupport ω ⊆ V, |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for every x, and |ω(x) − g(x)| ≤ ε for every x ∈ ℝ^P.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (V : Set (Euclid P)) (g : Euclid P → Covector (Euclid P) n) (ε : ℝ), IsOpen V → Continuous g → HasCompactSupport g → tsupport g ⊆ V → (∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm (g x) ≤ 1) → 0 < ε → ∃ ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n, IsTestForm ω ∧ tsupport ω ⊆ V ∧ (∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm (ω x) ≤ 1) ∧ ∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm (ω x - g x) ≤ ε
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: this is the comparator-accepted theorem of DAG node root.density_one_implies_regular-a1.imrep_mass_and_support-a1.smooth_unit_approximation-a1.mollify_unit_field-a1 (candidate 8abce32), reused with its identical frozen type. It is the mollification g_σ := g̃ ∗ φ_σ of the selected proof (step 3). The proof below reproduces the accepted Lean proof. That proof normalizes a ContDiffBump kernel explicitly, because Mathlib's ContDiffBump.normed is outside the import closure of GMT.Ch07.Submission, and here the coefficient map is written out instead of being cited from that node's own prerequisite coeff_norm_rep.
Notation: Λ := Covector (Euclid P) n with its operator norm ‖·‖; |·| := covectorEuclideanNorm; e is the standard orthonormal basis of ℝ^P and e_I := (e_{I 0}, …, e_{I(n−1)}) for I : Fin n → Fin P.
1. (Coefficient map.) For I : Fin n → Fin P let c_I : Λ → ℝ be α ↦ α(e_I) if I is strictly increasing, and the zero functional otherwise. Each c_I is continuous linear, since evaluation of a continuous alternating map at a fixed tuple is. Let A : Λ → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n → Fin P), Aα := (c_I(α))_I; A is continuous linear. By EuclideanSpace.norm_eq, ‖Aα‖ = √(∑_I c_I(α)²). Termwise, c_I(α)² = (if StrictMono I then α(e_I)² else 0), which is the summand in the definition of covectorEuclideanNorm. Hence |α| = ‖Aα‖ for every α. Put C₀ := ‖A‖ ≥ 0 (operator norm). Then |α| ≤ C₀‖α‖ for every α.
2. (Support margin.) tsupport g is compact (g has compact support) and contained in the open set V. So there is r > 0 with cthickening(r, tsupport g) ⊆ V (IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open).
3. (Uniform continuity.) g is continuous with compact support, hence uniformly continuous (HasCompactSupport.uniformContinuous_of_continuous). Choose s₀ > 0 with ‖g(y) − g(x)‖ < ε/(C₀ + 1) whenever dist(y, x) < s₀. Put s := min(s₀, r) > 0.
4. (Kernel.) Let φ be the smooth bump function (ContDiffBump) centred at 0 ∈ ℝ^P with inner radius s/2 and outer radius s. Then φ is C^∞, 0 ≤ φ, support φ = B(0, s), and φ is continuous with compact support, hence integrable. J := ∫ φ > 0: φ ≥ 0 is integrable and its support B(0, s) has positive Lebesgue measure (integral_pos_iff_support_of_nonneg, measure_ball_pos). Put ψ := φ/J. Then ψ is C^∞, ψ ≥ 0 and ∫ ψ = J/J = 1. If φ(y) = 0 then ψ(y) = 0, so support ψ ⊆ support φ = B(0, s), and ψ has compact support.
5. (Definition.) Let ω := ψ ⋆ g, that is ω(x) = ∫ ψ(t)•g(x − t) dt (convolution ψ g (lsmul ℝ ℝ) volume), a Bochner integral in the complete space Λ. g is continuous, hence locally integrable, and ψ is continuous with compact support. So the convolution exists at every x (HasCompactSupport.convolutionExists_left), i.e. each integrand t ↦ ψ(t)•g(x − t) is integrable.
6. (IsTestForm ω.) ω is C^∞ (HasCompactSupport.contDiff_convolution_left: ψ is C^∞ with compact support and g is locally integrable). ω has compact support (HasCompactSupport.convolution: ψ and g both have compact support).
7. (tsupport ω ⊆ V.) support ω ⊆ support ψ + support g (support_convolution_subset). Let y = t + z with t ∈ support ψ ⊆ B(0, s) and z ∈ support g ⊆ tsupport g. Then dist(y, z) = ‖t‖ < s, so y ∈ thickening(s, tsupport g). Hence tsupport ω ⊆ closure(thickening(s, tsupport g)) ⊆ cthickening(s, tsupport g) ⊆ cthickening(r, tsupport g) ⊆ V, using s ≤ r and step 2.
8. (|ω| ≤ 1.) Fix x. A is continuous linear and the integrand of step 5 is integrable. So A commutes with the integral (ContinuousLinearMap.integral_comp_comm) and with scalar multiplication: A(ω(x)) = ∫ ψ(t)•A(g(x − t)) dt = (ψ ⋆ (A∘g))(x). Here ψ ≥ 0, ∫ ψ = 1, support ψ ⊆ B(0, s), A∘g is continuous (hence a.e.-strongly measurable), and dist(A(g(y)), 0) = ‖A(g(y))‖ = |g(y)| ≤ 1 for every y. The averaging estimate dist_convolution_le therefore gives dist((ψ ⋆ (A∘g))(x), 0) ≤ 1. Hence |ω(x)| = ‖A(ω(x))‖ ≤ 1.
9. (Approximation.) Fix x. For every y ∈ B(x, s), dist(y, x) < s ≤ s₀, so ‖g(y) − g(x)‖ < ε/(C₀ + 1) by step 3. dist_convolution_le, applied with the same ψ, the a.e.-strongly measurable g and the centre g(x), gives ‖ω(x) − g(x)‖ = dist(ω(x), g(x)) ≤ ε/(C₀ + 1). By step 1, |ω(x) − g(x)| = ‖A(ω(x) − g(x))‖ ≤ C₀‖ω(x) − g(x)‖ ≤ C₀ε/(C₀ + 1) ≤ ε.
10. Steps 6–9 show IsTestForm ω, tsupport ω ⊆ V, |ω(x)| ≤ 1 and |ω(x) − g(x)| ≤ ε for every x ∈ ℝ^P.
proof_key_steps: The coefficient map A, Aα = (α(e_I))_{I increasing}, gives |α| = ‖Aα‖ ≤ ‖A‖·‖α‖.
Choose r > 0 with cthickening(r, tsupport g) ⊆ V; by uniform continuity choose s₀ > 0 with ‖g(y) − g(x)‖ < ε/(‖A‖+1) when dist(y, x) < s₀, and put s := min(s₀, r).
Normalize a smooth bump of outer radius s explicitly: ψ := φ/∫φ is C^∞, ψ ≥ 0, ∫ψ = 1, support ψ ⊆ B(0, s), compact support.
ω := ψ ⋆ g is C^∞ with compact support and tsupport ω ⊆ cthickening(s, tsupport g) ⊆ V.
A commutes with the integral, so dist_convolution_le gives |ω(x)| = ‖(ψ ⋆ (A∘g))(x)‖ ≤ 1.
dist_convolution_le gives ‖ω(x) − g(x)‖ ≤ ε/(‖A‖+1), hence |ω(x) − g(x)| ≤ ‖A‖ε/(‖A‖+1) ≤ ε.

subproblems.title: Uniform approximation of continuous compactly supported covector fields by test forms supported in an open set (selected proof, step 3)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n, d ∈ ℕ and let c : Λ := Covector (Euclid P) n → ℝ^d = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) be a continuous linear equivalence with covectorEuclideanNorm α = ‖c α‖ for every α ∈ Λ. Let V ⊆ ℝ^P be open, let G : ℝ^P → Λ be continuous with compact support and tsupport G ⊆ V, and let ε > 0. Then there is an n-form ω : ℝ^P → Λ that is C^∞ with compact support (IsTestForm ω), with tsupport ω ⊆ V and covectorEuclideanNorm (ω(x) − G(x)) ≤ ε for every x ∈ ℝ^P.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n d : ℕ) (c : Covector (Euclid P) n ≃L[ℝ] EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) (V : Set (Euclid P)) (G : Euclid P → Covector (Euclid P) n) (ε : ℝ), (∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, covectorEuclideanNorm α = ‖c α‖) → IsOpen V → Continuous G → HasCompactSupport G → tsupport G ⊆ V → 0 < ε → ∃ ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n, IsTestForm ω ∧ tsupport ω ⊆ V ∧ ∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm (ω x - G x) ≤ ε
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: selected proof, step 3, first bullet (approximating sequences): the rescaling argument around the sibling mollify_unit_field, stated for an arbitrary open set V and a single error ε > 0. In the selected proof, V = W and G = g̃.
Notation: Λ := Covector (Euclid P) n; |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α = ‖c α‖ (hypothesis). For F : ℝ^P → Λ and t ∈ ℝ, t•F is the pointwise multiple x ↦ t•F(x).
1. (Homogeneity.) For t ∈ ℝ and α ∈ Λ, |t•α| = ‖c(t•α)‖ = ‖t•c(α)‖ = |t|·‖c(α)‖ = |t|·|α|, because c is linear.
2. (Bound for G.) The map c∘G : ℝ^P → ℝ^d is continuous. Since c(0) = 0, support(c∘G) ⊆ support G, so c∘G has compact support (HasCompactSupport.comp_left). A continuous compactly supported map into a normed space is bounded (HasCompactSupport.exists_bound_of_continuous): there is C ∈ ℝ with ‖c(G(x))‖ ≤ C for all x. Put s := max(C, 0) + 1. Then s ≥ 1 > 0 and |G(x)| = ‖c(G(x))‖ ≤ C ≤ max(C, 0) ≤ s for every x.
3. (Normalized field.) Let g(x) := s⁻¹•G(x). g is continuous, as a constant multiple of a continuous map. If g(x) ≠ 0 then G(x) ≠ 0, so support g ⊆ support G. Hence g has compact support (HasCompactSupport.mono), and tsupport g ⊆ tsupport G ⊆ V. By steps 1–2, |g(x)| = s⁻¹·|G(x)| ≤ s⁻¹·s = 1 for every x.
4. (Mollification.) Apply the sibling mollify_unit_field (dor_ims_sua_mollify_unit_field) to P, n, the open set V, the field g and the positive number ε/s. Its hypotheses hold: V is open by assumption, the conditions on g were verified in step 3, and ε/s > 0 because ε > 0 and s > 0. It gives an n-form ω₀ with IsTestForm ω₀, tsupport ω₀ ⊆ V and |ω₀(x) − g(x)| ≤ ε/s for every x. Its further conclusion |ω₀| ≤ 1 is not needed.
5. (Rescaling.) Put ω := s•ω₀ (pointwise). ω is C^∞ because ω₀ is (a constant multiple of a C^∞ map), and ω has compact support because ω₀ does (HasCompactSupport.smul_left). So IsTestForm ω. Also tsupport ω ⊆ tsupport ω₀ ⊆ V (tsupport_smul_subset_right).
6. (Error.) For every x, ω(x) − G(x) = s•ω₀(x) − s•(s⁻¹•G(x)) = s•(ω₀(x) − g(x)), using s·s⁻¹ = 1 and linearity. By step 1 and s > 0, |ω(x) − G(x)| = s·|ω₀(x) − g(x)| ≤ s·(ε/s) = ε.
7. By steps 5 and 6, ω satisfies IsTestForm ω, tsupport ω ⊆ V and covectorEuclideanNorm (ω(x) − G(x)) ≤ ε for all x ∈ ℝ^P.
proof_key_steps: |t•α| = |t|·|α| because |·| = ‖c ·‖ and c is linear.
c∘G is continuous with compact support, hence bounded by some C; put s := max(C, 0) + 1 > 0, so |G| ≤ s.
g := s⁻¹•G is continuous, compactly supported, tsupport g ⊆ V and |g| ≤ 1.
mollify_unit_field applied to g with error ε/s gives a test form ω₀ with tsupport ω₀ ⊆ V and |ω₀ − g| ≤ ε/s.
ω := s•ω₀ is a test form with tsupport ω ⊆ V and |ω − G| = s·|ω₀ − g| ≤ ε.

subproblems.title: Limit of T along test forms converging uniformly with supports in a fixed W ⊂⊂ U (selected proof, steps 4–5)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n, d ∈ ℕ and let c : Λ := Covector (Euclid P) n → ℝ^d = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) be a continuous linear equivalence with |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α = ‖c α‖ for every α ∈ Λ. Let U ⊆ ℝ^P be any set, T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n), and m : Set(ℝ^P) → ℝ any function such that |T(ω)| ≤ r·m(W) whenever W ⊆ ℝ^P is open with W ⊂⊂ U (CompactlyContained W U: closure W is compact and contained in U), ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) (TestFormOn U n), tsupport ω ⊆ W, r ∈ ℝ and |ω(x)| ≤ r for all x. Then there is Φ : (ℝ^P → Λ) → ℝ such that T(ω_k) → Φ(G) as k → ∞ whenever G : ℝ^P → Λ, W ⊆ ℝ^P is open with W ⊂⊂ U, (ω_k) is a sequence in TestFormOn U n with tsupport ω_k ⊆ W for every k, and (ε_k) is a real sequence with ε_k → 0 and |ω_k(x) − G(x)| ≤ ε_k for all k and x.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n d : ℕ) (c : Covector (Euclid P) n ≃L[ℝ] EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (m : Set (Euclid P) → ℝ), (∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, covectorEuclideanNorm α = ‖c α‖) → (∀ (W : Set (Euclid P)) (ω : TestFormOn U n) (r : ℝ), IsOpen W → CompactlyContained W U → tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) ⊆ W → (∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x) ≤ r) → |T ω| ≤ r * m W) → ∃ Φ : (Euclid P → Covector (Euclid P) n) → ℝ, ∀ (G : Euclid P → Covector (Euclid P) n) (W : Set (Euclid P)) (ωs : ℕ → TestFormOn U n) (εs : ℕ → ℝ), IsOpen W → CompactlyContained W U → (∀ k, tsupport (ωs k : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) ⊆ W) → (∀ k x, covectorEuclideanNorm ((ωs k : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x - G x) ≤ εs k) → Tendsto εs atTop (𝓝 0) → Tendsto (fun k => T (ωs k)) atTop (𝓝 (Φ G))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: selected proof, steps 4 (Cauchy estimate) and 5 (definition of L(g) as a limit). In the selected proof G = g̃ and m(W) = (M_W(T)).toReal. The selected node itself discharges the hypothesis on m with its prerequisite eval_mass_bound (cmr_abs_apply_le_massOn), which this child does not use. Here G is an arbitrary map ℝ^P → Λ and m an arbitrary function with the stated bound.
Notation: Λ := Covector (Euclid P) n; |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α = ‖c α‖ (hypothesis); 'W ⊂⊂ U' means CompactlyContained W U, i.e. closure W is compact and closure W ⊆ U. Elements of TestFormOn U n are identified with their underlying forms; TestFormOn U n is a real vector subspace of the n-forms, and T (through T.toCurrent) is linear on it. For G : ℝ^P → Λ, a triple D = (W, (ω_k), (ε_k)), with W ⊆ ℝ^P, ω_k ∈ TestFormOn U n and ε_k ∈ ℝ, is approximating data for G if: W is open; W ⊂⊂ U; tsupport ω_k ⊆ W for every k; |ω_k(x) − G(x)| ≤ ε_k for all k and x; and ε_k → 0.
1. (Triangle inequality.) For α, β ∈ Λ, |α − β| = ‖c(α) − c(β)‖ ≤ ‖c(α)‖ + ‖c(β)‖ = |α| + |β|, because c is linear.
2. (Unions.) Let W and W' be open with W ⊂⊂ U and W' ⊂⊂ U. Then W ∪ W' is open. Also closure(W ∪ W') = closure W ∪ closure W' is compact (a union of two compact sets) and contained in U. So W ∪ W' ⊂⊂ U.
3. (Key estimate.) Let D = (W, (ω_k), (ε_k)) and D' = (W', (ω'_l), (ε'_l)) be approximating data for the same G. Then for all k, l: |T(ω_k) − T(ω'_l)| ≤ (ε_k + ε'_l)·m(W ∪ W').
 Proof. Fix k, l and put δ := ω_k − ω'_l ∈ TestFormOn U n; as a form, δ(x) = ω_k(x) − ω'_l(x).
 - Support. If x ∉ support ω_k ∪ support ω'_l, then δ(x) = 0 − 0 = 0. So support δ ⊆ support ω_k ∪ support ω'_l. Taking closures, tsupport δ ⊆ closure(support ω_k ∪ support ω'_l) = tsupport ω_k ∪ tsupport ω'_l ⊆ W ∪ W'.
 - Size. For every x, δ(x) = (ω_k(x) − G(x)) − (ω'_l(x) − G(x)). By step 1, |δ(x)| ≤ |ω_k(x) − G(x)| + |ω'_l(x) − G(x)| ≤ ε_k + ε'_l.
 - Bound. By step 2, W ∪ W' is open and W ∪ W' ⊂⊂ U. The hypothesis on m, applied to W ∪ W', δ and r := ε_k + ε'_l, gives |T(δ)| ≤ (ε_k + ε'_l)·m(W ∪ W').
 Finally, T(δ) = T(ω_k) − T(ω'_l) because T is linear.
4. (Convergence.) Let D = (W, (ω_k), (ε_k)) be approximating data for G and put a_k := T(ω_k). Then (a_k) converges in ℝ.
 Proof. Put μ := |m(W ∪ W)| ≥ 0. Let η > 0 and θ := η/(2(μ + 1)) > 0. Since ε_k → 0, also |ε_k| → 0, so there is N with |ε_k| < θ for all k ≥ N. Let k ≥ N. Step 3, with D' := D and l := N, gives
 |a_k − a_N| ≤ (ε_k + ε_N)·m(W ∪ W) ≤ |(ε_k + ε_N)·m(W ∪ W)| = |ε_k + ε_N|·μ ≤ (|ε_k| + |ε_N|)·μ ≤ 2θ·μ = η·μ/(μ + 1) < η.
 Here |ε_k| + |ε_N| < 2θ, μ ≥ 0, and the last inequality holds because η > 0 and μ < μ + 1. So for every η > 0 there is N with dist(a_k, a_N) < η for all k ≥ N; that is, (a_k) is a Cauchy sequence (Metric.cauchySeq_iff'). Since ℝ is complete, (a_k) converges (cauchySeq_tendsto_of_complete).
5. (Definition of Φ.) Let G : ℝ^P → Λ. If G admits approximating data, choose one such triple D_G = (W_G, (ω^G_k), (ε^G_k)) (axiom of choice). By step 4 the sequence (T(ω^G_k))_k converges; let Φ(G) be (a chosen) limit of it. Otherwise set Φ(G) := 0. Then T(ω^G_k) → Φ(G) whenever D_G is defined.
6. (Every approximating sequence tends to Φ(G).) Let G, W, (ω_k) and (ε_k) satisfy the hypotheses of the conclusion: W is open, W ⊂⊂ U, tsupport ω_k ⊆ W for every k, |ω_k(x) − G(x)| ≤ ε_k for all k and x, and ε_k → 0. These say exactly that D := (W, (ω_k), (ε_k)) is approximating data for G. So D_G exists, and T(ω^G_k) → Φ(G) by step 5. Step 3, applied to D and D_G with l = k, gives 0 ≤ |T(ω_k) − T(ω^G_k)| ≤ (ε_k + ε^G_k)·m(W ∪ W_G) for every k. The right-hand side tends to (0 + 0)·m(W ∪ W_G) = 0. By the squeeze principle, T(ω_k) − T(ω^G_k) → 0. Hence T(ω_k) = (T(ω_k) − T(ω^G_k)) + T(ω^G_k) → 0 + Φ(G) = Φ(G).
7. So Φ has the required property.
proof_key_steps: |·| = ‖c ·‖ satisfies the triangle inequality, and W ∪ W' is open and ⊂⊂ U when W, W' are open and ⊂⊂ U.
For two approximating data of the same G, the m-hypothesis applied to ω_k − ω'_l on W ∪ W' with r = ε_k + ε'_l gives |T(ω_k) − T(ω'_l)| ≤ (ε_k + ε'_l)·m(W ∪ W').
With equal data this makes (T(ω_k)) Cauchy, hence convergent in ℝ.
Define Φ(G) as the limit along chosen approximating data (0 if none exists).
The estimate with l = k squeezes T(ω_k) − T(ω^G_k) to 0, so every approximating sequence of G has limit Φ(G).

subproblems.title: Linear extension of a locally bounded current to compactly supported continuous covector fields on ℝ^P (selected proof, steps 2–3, 5–8)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n, d ∈ ℕ and let c : Λ := Covector (Euclid P) n → ℝ^d = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) be a continuous linear equivalence with |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α = ‖c α‖ for every α ∈ Λ. Let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open, T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n), and m : Set(ℝ^P) → ℝ a function such that |T(ω)| ≤ r·m(W) whenever W ⊆ ℝ^P is open with W ⊂⊂ U (CompactlyContained W U: closure W is compact and contained in U), ω ∈ TestFormOn U n, tsupport ω ⊆ W, r ∈ ℝ and |ω(x)| ≤ r for all x. Then there is Φ : (ℝ^P → Λ) → ℝ such that: (a) Φ(G₁ + G₂) = Φ(G₁) + Φ(G₂) whenever G₁, G₂ : ℝ^P → Λ are continuous with compact support and tsupport G_i ⊆ U; (b) Φ(t•G) = t·Φ(G) for every t ∈ ℝ and every continuous compactly supported G : ℝ^P → Λ with tsupport G ⊆ U; (c) Φ(ω) = T(ω) for every ω ∈ TestFormOn U n (ω regarded as the map ℝ^P → Λ); (d) |Φ(G)| ≤ r·m(W) whenever W ⊆ ℝ^P is open with W ⊂⊂ U, G : ℝ^P → Λ is continuous with compact support and tsupport G ⊆ W, r ∈ ℝ, and |G(x)| ≤ r for all x.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n d : ℕ) (c : Covector (Euclid P) n ≃L[ℝ] EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (m : Set (Euclid P) → ℝ), IsOpen U → (∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, covectorEuclideanNorm α = ‖c α‖) → (∀ (W : Set (Euclid P)) (ω : TestFormOn U n) (r : ℝ), IsOpen W → CompactlyContained W U → tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) ⊆ W → (∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x) ≤ r) → |T ω| ≤ r * m W) → ∃ Φ : (Euclid P → Covector (Euclid P) n) → ℝ, (∀ G₁ G₂ : Euclid P → Covector (Euclid P) n, Continuous G₁ → HasCompactSupport G₁ → tsupport G₁ ⊆ U → Continuous G₂ → HasCompactSupport G₂ → tsupport G₂ ⊆ U → Φ (G₁ + G₂) = Φ G₁ + Φ G₂) ∧ (∀ (t : ℝ) (G : Euclid P → Covector (Euclid P) n), Continuous G → HasCompactSupport G → tsupport G ⊆ U → Φ (t • G) = t * Φ G) ∧ (∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, Φ (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) = T ω) ∧ ∀ (W : Set (Euclid P)) (G : Euclid P → Covector (Euclid P) n) (r : ℝ), IsOpen W → CompactlyContained W U → Continuous G → HasCompactSupport G → tsupport G ⊆ W → (∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm (G x) ≤ r) → |Φ G| ≤ r * m W
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: selected proof, steps 2 (admissible open sets), 3 (approximating sequences), 5–6 (definition and linearity), 7 (agreement with T) and 8 (local bound). They are carried out on ℝ^P for compactly supported continuous covector fields G; in the selected proof G = g̃. The bound (M_W(T)).toReal is abstracted to m. For (d), the selected step 8 bounds T on unit-size approximants ±ω_k by le_massOn. Here the m-hypothesis is applied to approximants of size r + 1/(k+1); in the selected node, m(W) = (M_W(T)).toReal and the m-hypothesis is supplied by eval_mass_bound (cmr_abs_apply_le_massOn), which is derived from le_massOn by rescaling. The selected node discharges the hypothesis on m; this child does not use eval_mass_bound.
Notation: Λ := Covector (Euclid P) n; |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α = ‖c α‖ (hypothesis). Since c is linear, |α + β| = ‖c(α) + c(β)‖ ≤ |α| + |β| and |t•α| = ‖t•c(α)‖ = |t|·|α|. 'W ⊂⊂ U' means CompactlyContained W U. Sums and real multiples of maps ℝ^P → Λ are pointwise. Elements of TestFormOn U n are identified with their underlying forms; TestFormOn U n is a real vector subspace of the n-forms, and T is linear on it.
1. (Choice of Φ.) The hypotheses on c and m are exactly those of the sibling limit_functional (dimred_mbl_fnd_tfe_exists_limit_functional) for (P, n, d, c, U, T, m). It gives Φ : (ℝ^P → Λ) → ℝ with the following property (L). Let G : ℝ^P → Λ, let W be open with W ⊂⊂ U, and let ω_k ∈ TestFormOn U n with tsupport ω_k ⊆ W. Suppose |ω_k(x) − G(x)| ≤ ε_k for all k and x, where ε_k → 0. Then T(ω_k) → Φ(G). Steps 4–7 prove (a)–(d) for this Φ.
2. (Topological facts.)
 (i) If S ⊆ U is compact, there is an open W with S ⊆ W and W ⊂⊂ U. As in the selected step 2: choose δ > 0 with cthickening(δ, S) ⊆ U (IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open; U is open) and put W := thickening(δ/2, S). W is open and S ⊆ W since δ/2 > 0. Also closure W ⊆ cthickening(δ/2, S) ⊆ cthickening(δ, S) ⊆ U, and cthickening(δ/2, S) is compact because S is compact and ℝ^P is proper; so closure W, a closed subset of it, is compact. Thus W ⊂⊂ U. (Mathlib's exists_open_between_and_isCompact_closure, for the locally compact regular space ℝ^P, gives the same W directly.)
 (ii) If W₁ and W₂ are open with W₁ ⊂⊂ U and W₂ ⊂⊂ U, then W₁ ∪ W₂ is open and W₁ ∪ W₂ ⊂⊂ U, since closure(W₁ ∪ W₂) = closure W₁ ∪ closure W₂ is compact and contained in U.
 (iii) If W ⊂⊂ U, then W ⊆ closure W ⊆ U.
 (iv) 1/(k+1) → 0 as k → ∞.
3. (Approximating sequences.) Let W be open with W ⊂⊂ U, and let G be continuous with compact support and tsupport G ⊆ W. For each k, the sibling uniform_approx (dimred_mbl_fnd_tfe_uniform_testForm_approx), applied with c, V := W, G and ε := 1/(k+1) > 0, gives a form ω_k with IsTestForm ω_k, tsupport ω_k ⊆ W and |ω_k(x) − G(x)| ≤ 1/(k+1) for all x. By 2(iii), tsupport ω_k ⊆ U, so ω_k ∈ TestFormOn U n. By 2(iv) and (L), T(ω_k) → Φ(G). If instead G is continuous with compact support and tsupport G ⊆ U, then tsupport G is compact. So 2(i) gives an open W ⊂⊂ U with tsupport G ⊆ W, and the above applies to this W.
4. (Additivity (a).) Let G₁ and G₂ be continuous with compact support and tsupport G_i ⊆ U. By step 3, for i = 1, 2 choose an open W_i ⊂⊂ U and ω^i_k ∈ TestFormOn U n with tsupport ω^i_k ⊆ W_i, |ω^i_k(x) − G_i(x)| ≤ 1/(k+1) and T(ω^i_k) → Φ(G_i). Put σ_k := ω¹_k + ω²_k ∈ TestFormOn U n.
 - tsupport σ_k ⊆ tsupport ω¹_k ∪ tsupport ω²_k ⊆ W₁ ∪ W₂ (tsupport_add), and W₁ ∪ W₂ is open and ⊂⊂ U by 2(ii).
 - For every x, σ_k(x) − (G₁ + G₂)(x) = (ω¹_k(x) − G₁(x)) + (ω²_k(x) − G₂(x)). Hence |σ_k(x) − (G₁ + G₂)(x)| ≤ 1/(k+1) + 1/(k+1), which tends to 0.
 By (L), T(σ_k) → Φ(G₁ + G₂). Since T is linear, T(σ_k) = T(ω¹_k) + T(ω²_k) → Φ(G₁) + Φ(G₂). Limits in ℝ are unique, so Φ(G₁ + G₂) = Φ(G₁) + Φ(G₂).
5. (Homogeneity (b).) Let G be continuous with compact support and tsupport G ⊆ U, and let t ∈ ℝ. Take W and ω_k as in step 3, so T(ω_k) → Φ(G). Then t•ω_k ∈ TestFormOn U n and tsupport(t•ω_k) ⊆ tsupport ω_k ⊆ W (tsupport_smul_subset_right). For every x, (t•ω_k)(x) − (t•G)(x) = t•(ω_k(x) − G(x)). So |(t•ω_k)(x) − (t•G)(x)| = |t|·|ω_k(x) − G(x)| ≤ |t|·(1/(k+1)), which tends to 0. By (L), T(t•ω_k) → Φ(t•G). By linearity, T(t•ω_k) = t·T(ω_k) → t·Φ(G). By uniqueness of limits, Φ(t•G) = t·Φ(G).
6. (Agreement (c).) Let ω ∈ TestFormOn U n. Then IsTestForm ω, so ω has compact support and tsupport ω is compact; also tsupport ω ⊆ U. By 2(i), choose an open W ⊂⊂ U with tsupport ω ⊆ W. For G := ω, take the constant sequence ω_k := ω with errors ε_k := 0. It satisfies the hypotheses of (L), since |ω(x) − ω(x)| = |0| = 0 ≤ 0. So the constant sequence T(ω) tends to Φ(ω). It also tends to T(ω), so Φ(ω) = T(ω) by uniqueness of limits.
7. (Bound (d).) Let W be open with W ⊂⊂ U, let G be continuous with compact support and tsupport G ⊆ W, let r ∈ ℝ, and let |G(x)| ≤ r for all x. Step 3, applied to W and G, gives ω_k ∈ TestFormOn U n with tsupport ω_k ⊆ W, |ω_k(x) − G(x)| ≤ 1/(k+1) and T(ω_k) → Φ(G). For every x, ω_k(x) = (ω_k(x) − G(x)) + G(x), so |ω_k(x)| ≤ 1/(k+1) + r. The hypothesis on m, applied to W, ω_k and r + 1/(k+1), gives |T(ω_k)| ≤ (r + 1/(k+1))·m(W) for every k. As k → ∞, |T(ω_k)| → |Φ(G)| (continuity of the absolute value) and (r + 1/(k+1))·m(W) → r·m(W). Non-strict inequalities are preserved under limits, so |Φ(G)| ≤ r·m(W).
8. Steps 4–7 prove (a)–(d) for Φ.
proof_key_steps: Take Φ from limit_functional: T(ω_k) → Φ(G) along every sequence of test forms approximating G uniformly with supports in a fixed open W ⊂⊂ U.
Every compact S ⊆ U lies in an open W ⊂⊂ U, and unions of two such sets are open and ⊂⊂ U.
uniform_approx with errors 1/(k+1) gives an approximating sequence in TestFormOn U n for every continuous compactly supported G with tsupport G ⊆ W.
Sums and real multiples of approximating sequences approximate G₁ + G₂ (on W₁ ∪ W₂) and t•G, so (a) and (b) follow from linearity of T and uniqueness of limits.
The constant sequence ω gives Φ(ω) = T(ω).
|ω_k| ≤ r + 1/(k+1) and the m-hypothesis give |T(ω_k)| ≤ (r + 1/(k+1))·m(W), hence |Φ(G)| ≤ r·m(W) in the limit.
